From Ken Stearn, FIFE

I am desperate for a supply of
thermal paper for my Brother HR5
printer. I wrote to W.A.V.E.  in
Barrow-in-Furness,which you gave
as a supplier but I have not had
any response. perhaps you could
publish this in the hope that
some of your readers may help.

"Thermal Brother A4 width sheets
(100 pack)x5 packs for `10 + `6

Surrey GU7 1XX (Tel:0483 860238)

From Raymond Hoy,  BASINGSTOKE


Dear Brian & Ron,

I have found your tabloid print
routine so much better for
printing text files than earlier
methods. Which bring me to the
question....how can I use it to
print my Tasword files in this
way? I presume I would have to
reSAVE files at a different
address and possibily rename
them then load into the OUTPRINT
program that's on OUTLET EXTRA
1. As I am not that good at
programming could this be
answered within Outlet as I am
sure it must be of use to other
readers for the same reasons.

Concerning Donald Pemberton's
problem (OUTLET 34) I have a
Brother M1009 printer and Handy-
type works alright on mine,with
a 128 and Disciple connected,
although the program take a bit
of getting used to.

When can we look forward to
OUTLET EXTRA 2 - that's if you
plan to do one?

Oh well,I am now looking forward
to receiving my July issue of
OUTLET like I have all the
others. Thats my way of saying
"Well done!" on a well-presented
and varied monthly magazine.

        Raymond Hoy

To Raymond Hoy from Brian

All credit must go to Mike Haine
who wrote TABLOID. OUTLET text
files are compressed and TABLOID
includes a decompressor so can't
be used on Tasword files without
quite a bit of re-writing. There
is also the fact that TABLOID is
3 columns of 32 characters but
default Tasword 2 files are 64
characters. I'm writing to Mike
Haine to see if he can come up
with any new program, meanwhile,
may I draw your attention to
TWOCOL in OUTLET 29 which prints
out two columns of 64 characters
each from Tasword files.

OUTLET EXTRA 2 is likely to be
many months away because of lack
of spare time! Sorry!    - Brian

From Andy Fleming, WILTSHIRE

Greetings to the brothers Cavers
and my thanks to you and all who
contribute to Outlet.

I would like to pass on a piece
of good fortune which occurred
as a direct result of an Outlet
program. Speclist,Issue 13,moved
me to write to several publish-
ers to enlarge my library.

Glentop,Shiva and Sunshine have
moved from the addresses I had
or gone out of business. Inter-
face Publications replied with
an order form listing all their
current holdings of Spectrum-
oriented books. The good news is

I can't remember all the books

but I ordered and received...

"Putting your Spectrum to work"
by Chris Callender

"Delving deeper into your ZX
Spectrum" by Dilwyn Jones

"Exploring artificial intelli-
gence on your Spectrum+ and
Spectrum" by Tim Hartnell

erence guide" by Richard Ross-
Langley.

wants to expand their library

     Interface Publications
    9-11 Kensington High St.

It is worth pointing out that

[letter undated but about early

Many thanks, Andy.     - Brian

From Dick Chappell, BELFAST

Dear Fellows,

Did you ever find a suitable
storage method for cartridges?
The enclosed label is full-size
for the pack in which it came -
a clear plastic box with hinged
lid, containing FERRERO ROCHER
whirls.

The trick is to persuade all
your womenfolk that they really
should treat themselves to a box
of this delightful confection.
Then, if you are like me, you
finish up buying them all one
(birthdays and Christmases...
takes years!) until you have the
number you want.

Each box holds 32, allowing one
eighth-inch divider down the
centre, compartment separators
and a label-sized rectangle of
polystyrene on which to stand
the cartridges.
              - Dick Chappell


Thanks, Dick. I use ice-cube
trays myself stood in those tape
cassette drawers you can buy -
not cheap though but I'd need
over 20 FERRERO ROCHER boxes to
store my cartridges and, as the
handwritten footnote (by your
wife I should think) to your
letter says, would end up with
FAT womenfolk! I'll settle for
lukewarm drinks.
                      - Brian

From Frank Harrop, BRIGHTON

Dear Brian and Ron,

At the moment I only have the
basic SAM with a single disk
drive and am waiting before I
buy any more items such as the
printer interface and/or extra
memory. As I wanted to print out
one item I borrowed Opus 34 from
Peter Bell (as we keep in touch)
and I do congratulate the "team"
on the Tabloid print out - it
really is first class and hope-
fully will arrive for the SAM in
due course.

Can I raise just one small point
on that? It is fine if you are
using continuous paper but on my

Brother M1109 printer the "paper
empty" operates and cuts off the
bottom line so that line appears
on the top of the next page
followed by the "skip" spaces.
Doesn't half make it odd to
read! It would help if you could
possibly include the usual Epson
"ignore paper empty" code unless
it would complicate matters for
others?

           Sincerely,

          Frank Harrop

To Frank Harrop from Brian

Unfortunately yes! If I add the
code you'll get the line printed
but the text will then continue
to print on the platen before
you put in the next sheet. If I
put a PAUSE in the routine then
continuous sheet users will have
to keep pressing a key after all
pages.The answer is when insert-
ing each sheet, wind down the
paper a line or two so printing
starts higher on the page (or is
it impossible on your printer?).
Again, let us credit Mike Haine
for writing TABLOID.

I've looked to see if I can get
Tabloid to work on SAM but can
see no easy answer yet.
                      - Brian

From Veronica Petter, BRISTOL

I understand you must compress
OUTLET to fit it into or rather,
onto a microdrive cartridge and
I wondered if the compressor
program you use has ben on a
past issue of OUTLET as I am
anxious to obtain a copy. I have
a "computer" friend who has only
microdrive and it will make it
much easier for me to be able to
transfer a complete disc rather
than bits and pieces to him.

If I must purchase a compressor,
perhaps you could let me know of
a suitable one and where to get
it from - one that is not too
complicated to use as I am not
terribly bright on that sort of
thing.

Thank you for publishing my
KWIKWRITE program in OUTLET. It
certainly looks nice with the
headings you put on and I have
kept that copy as my main one
alhough I have now made it much
more idiot-proof and the warning
you inserted about the inputting
of finished arrays no longer
applies. I have been thinking of
re-submitting it but I am using
a smaller font which may not
work on other machines except
the Spectrum [48K?] (it is a 42
char-per-line font).

Oh yes, one other little thing,
could you please tell me or find
a good Samaritan to tell me, how
does one get the bits of machine
code into a program in the same


way as you do (I think on REM
lines) as it is much better and
more convenient than loading
fonts as I have to with my pro-
grams?

That's it then. Please excuse
the mistakes and lop-sided paper
(Woolworths can't even cut paper
square now!). Keep up with the
good work that OUTLET does. I
have learned a lot from it;
especially by studying your
methods of programming. My very
best wishes to both of you.

           Yours sincerely,

            Veronica Petter

To Veronica Petter from Brian

OUTLET is not compressed by one
method but by several and these
techniques are used on ALL the
versions of OUTLET - not just on
the microdrive version.The first
master of each issue is created
on two microdrive cartridges and
then converted for each system
shortly before publication.

This conversion involves change
of syntax and other pieces of
code so other versions will not
run on microdrive although some
individual programs might.

I must stress to all our readers
that only programs marked "FREE-
WARE" may be copied and given to
friends.

Apart from those, the whole of
OUTLET is copyright and must not
be copied (except as back up for
one's own use). Readers should
NEVER copy the whole of OUTLET
or ANY programs but FREEWARE for
someone else.

The only other exception is that
readers may use our routines in
their own programs and give away
or sell such programs but not
the original routine program.For
example,if someone wrote a data-
base program they could use our
DIMSORTER routine from Issue 23
to sort data WITHIN the database
program then distribute the
program for free or profit but
should not give away copies of
the original DIMSORTER program.

I'll be happy to put your new
version of KWIK-WRITE into ADD-
ENDERS so long as the 42 char
font routine is your own or you
have permission!

I'm being a real pain this month
aren't I but how else can I ever
get to be rich and famous and
live in a big house and drive a
Porsche and stuff?

Now, to put machine code, fonts
etc. into REMs, use REMSTORE
(OUTLET 6).I'm sorry this is not
available to +3 users but I hope
to include it in OUTLET EXTRA 2
one day. Meanwhile I can only
suggest buying the tape issue.

                       - Brian

From Ken Hunter, N. YORKS

Dear Ron,

I have a +2 and my printer (a
Brother M1109) is connnected
through the RS232/Midi port.This
means I can only address the
printer in 128K mode. I wonder
if there is any command I can
put through from the keyboard to
enable me to use the printer in
48K mode? At present, you see, I
cannot use the printer in
conjunction with Outlet, which
runs in 48K - for instance, to
print out pages of instructions
etc.
        Yours sincerely,

           Ken Hunter

To Ken Hunter from Brian
Have you tried OUTLET in 128K
mode recently as it is now more
compatible? If it still does not
work, press reset; enter 128K
BASIC; MERGE the "CONTENTS" and
enter 9984 RETURN and then RUN
the program. If it runs o.k. you
could try loading a text file
and printing it using the ZX-
printer option. To use TABLOID
you must change CLEAR #:OPEN #
etc. in line 1410 to the syntax
used by the +2 to send printer
codes. Look in your manual as I
do not have a +2. Then use the
Opus option. Another possibility
is to use your Interface 1 RS232
port if your cable fits or you
can get one made up. This works
in 48K mode. Let me know how you
get on.                - Brian

From Patrick Anderson, IPSWICH

Dear Ron and Brian,

Could you please inform me if
you have any program capable of
giving me a good screen dump to
my printer. I have a MANNESMANN
TALLY SPIRIT 80.

The various programs I've so far
tried have failed miserably. The
closest to success to date is
the FURNISHER prog (OUTLET 11).
However, this will only print
out about three quarters of the
picture leaving the bottom
quarter printout as garbish.This
applies if using the FURNISHER
program as it stands or loading
some other screen into the
program.

I've tried about everything I
know (which is very little as I
have no understanding of machine
code).HELP!If you've a cartridge
with a suitable program on then
please let me know.I'll send for
it post haste.

rate on the dip switches in your
printer(see manual)to say, 1200.
Check VERY carefully! Now try
FURNISHER again and enter 1200
for the baud rate. If this still
does NOT work I can only guess
there's a printer fault. If it
DOES work o.k. then remember you
must alter the baud rate in
programs like wordprocessors or
switch the dip switches back as
needed. Let me know how you get
on.                     - Brian

From Richard Armstrong, TELFORD



Dear Ron,

If it is the end of cartridges
soon I shall want to transfer
some of it to disc so do I
purchase the Disciple Interface
as I can transfer from cartridge
to disc or do I go for the new
SAM and disc drive? If I buy the
SAM, will I be able to transfer
from cartridge to SAM disc?

            Regards,

        Richard Armstrong

To Richard Armstrong from Brian

95%+ of Spectrum games will run
on SAM if you use EMUTILITY from
OUTLET 34 subject to your tape
recorder being suitable. I still
find many games just will not
load from one of my recorders.

However, without EMUTILITY, Only
the very simplest BASIC programs
will transfer without change.
For example, NO OUTLET programs
will convert without change and
only THREE of the very simplest
from the whole of Issue 35 would
convert even AFTER my best
efforts to rewrite them. Machine
code utilities rarely run. In
theory, most programs may be got
to work with a lot of skill and
experience but most people have


found little of their Spectrum
software (apart from commercial
games used with an emulator like
EMUTILITY) workable on SAM.

I should clarify that using an
emulator means loading in some
code and also possibly a copy of
the Spectrum ROM and setting
aside an area of the SAM COUPE's
memory to simulate a Spectrum
(but normally without disc or
printer access etc.). Whereas,
"converting" Spectrum programs
to SAM BASIC means using a
convertor to change a Spectrum
BASIC program actually into a
SAM BASIC program which runs as
a SAM program, can be SAVEd to
SAM disc, load files from disc,
be enhanced to use the extra SAM
features etc. etc.

In short, for all practical
purposes, don't expect much of
your cartridge software to be
used on SAM unless it is mostly
EXTREMELY simple BASIC. However,
if you are an enthusiastic
programmer and like experiment-
ing you may be able to transfer
the essence of some programs and
create a dramatically-improved
version on the SAM.

On the other hand, MOST of your
software can be got to run with
the Disciple. The advantage of
the SAM is that if the faults
can be sorted out it has some
super features with tremendous
potential - and ideal for the
old Spectrum hand to develop
further.

To further complicate things, I
hear microdrive cartridges will
continue to be produced (see
LOOKOUT!)so you may wish to stay
with microdrives - at least for
a while to see how the SAM
situation develops.

                        - Brian.

From Les Tyler, CHELTENHAM

First of all, I am a trifle
miffed! Having spent many happy,
(albeit frustrating!), hours at
the OERKEVAN game in Issue 23, I
actually got the thing out on
one occasion recently; all 4
suits nicely laid out. My cries
of joy and elation were somewhat
tempered, however,by the refusal
of the program to recognise this
outstanding achievement- it just
asked if I wanted to play again!

Somehow, I reckon the author did
not expect there to be anyone
around brilliant enough to
perform this amazing feat so he
did not put in any appropriate
comment!

I thought I'd put one in myself,
(who knows, I may solve it again
one day!) but it seems I'm not
that brilliant really as I have
not found out where the comment
should go as yet!Anyway,congrat-
ulations to the author (Danish,I
believe?) on a very good version
of a favourite old patience
game. I don't go for games as a
rule but I like this one.Perhaps
it is because I do not need to
have nimble fingers!

New topic. Can you, (or somebody
else out there), please write a
few notes about CP/M as it
applies to the Spectrum ? I have
often seen references to it but
virtually no comment on what is
actually available; the quality
of the software, etc.

I am considering getting another
128K machine to supplement my
present one and the +3 looks to
be the best bet as far as I am
concerned, apart from the 3-inch
disc set-up which is a bit of a
pain when I have a goodly coll-
ection of 5.25 discs! Any infor-
mation on CP/M would be greatly
appreciated. In particular, do
users think it worth the addit-
ional expense incurred getting a
+3 as opposed to a +1 or +2 with
DISCIPLE and separate drives
already to hand?

You will probably have gathered
I am not contemplating buying a
SAM Coupe! A few months ago I,
like many others, was eagerly
anticipating its arival on the
scene but having read all the


reviews and noted the various
hassles that others have had, I
feel even a fully operational
model would not have much in the
way of an advantage for my pur-
poses over a 128K Spectrum with
Beta Basic version 4.

Continuing with the SAM theme;
looking back through old OUTLET
editorials/letter files, I note
a certain B. Cavers is on record
as not being very pro-procedure
minded. The relevant comments
were, of course, written long
before SAM even remotely looked
like appearing in its finished
form [what's new? - an uncertain
B.C.] and I got to wondering
whether or not you had modified
your views at all,having had the
chance to play around at length

with the SAM's BASIC which is, I
gather,broadly in line with BETA
BASIC (Same author, of course).

I've always felt that procedures
were more elegant and easier to
use than ordinary subroutines
and consider that they would
have been a most useful addition
to the standard Spectrum ROM.
Still, one cannot put quarts
into pint pots, as they say, and
others can almost certainly name
other facilities they consider
ought to have been included.

Finally, I couldn't resist sub-
stituting the ITALICISER routine
for AUTOCHARS in JOTTER. Comes
out quite nicely,I think.Pity my
printer doesn't have bit-image
facilities! Cheers!  - Les.

To Les Tyler from Brian


Re: OERKENVAN, I plead guilty
with mitigating circumstances as
I had to extensively rewrite the
program (written in Danish) and
omitted part of the program that
gave the player 3 chances at the
game (some sort of reshuffle I
think) so you did AMAZINGLY well
to finish in one pass!

Re: PROCEDURES - NOT GUILTY! If
you re-read what I said you will
see I was attacking the common
assumption that procedures are
more "structural" than GO SUBs
whereas they are structurally
identical (both USE a subroutine
then continue from the branch).

I'm delighted with procedures. I
love procedures. I belong to the
Ultimate Heavenly Procedure
Association.I used procedures on
my Atari St Fast Basic until I
found GO SUBs were faster. Now,
on the SAM COUPE, procedures are
perfectly implemented as they do
not need the use of PROC to use
them and virtually give the
programmer a method of instantly
creating his own keywords.Ideal!

I'll leave it to someone more
knowledgeable to write on CP/M
(as we have only recently bought
it) except to say it has the
advantage of running programs
written on other computers in
CP/M but the disadvantage that
it uses the lowest common

demoninator of them all so there
are no graphics to speak of and
it cannot use special features
of a machine. We already have
some public domain programs that
will appear in ADD-ENDERS.

The high cost of 3" disc storage
on the +3 compared to 3.5"
(something like 5 times the cost
I reckon)not to mention the much
wider availability of 3.5" are
compelling reasons for buying a
Disciple rather than a +3.

                        - Brian

From Glenn Owens, BRISTOL

I have tried the latest solution
to the PROCROSS"pushed sideways"
problem [lower part of crossword
squares printed out too far to
right on Glenn's Citizen 120D
printer - B.C.] that you very
kindly sent me.As you can see it
has almost cured the problem. I
don't think you would get much
better than that. I attained the
best adjustment by setting GO=3
in line 5832. There is a SLIGHT
"pushed sideways"effect left but
3 was the best setting.

Many thanks for all the time you
have spent helping to solve this
problem.
               - Glenn Owens

To Glenn Owens from Brian

Glad all is now reasonably o.k.
Readers note:PROCROSS prints out
perfectly on true Epson-standard
printers but here's the solution
I gave Glenn if you also get the
lower part of squares printed
too far to the right. EDIT line
5830;renumber it 5835 and enter.
Enter(CHECK EVERY SEMI-COLON!):-

5830 IF M=N THEN LET GO=1
5832 IF GO=3 THEN LPRINT Z$;"Z";
CHR$ 1;CHR$ 0; CHR$ 1;:LET GO=0
5833 LET GO=GO+1

You may need to adjust the 3 in
GO=3 at line 5832. SAVE a FRESH
copy using the lines 9970 onward
[if deleted(see info) reload and
alter original again].  - Brian.

95%+ of Spectrum games will run on SAM if you use EMUTILITY from OUTLET 34 subject to your tape recorder being suitable. I still find many games just will not load from one of my recorders.

Machine code utilities rarely run. In theory, most programs may be got to work with a lot of skill and experience but most people have

I should clarify that using an emulator means loading in some code and also possibly a copy of the Spectrum ROM and setting aside an area of the SAM COUPE's memory to simulate a Spectrum (but normally without disc or printer access etc.). 95%+ игр Spectrum будут работать на SAM, если вы используете EMUTILITY из OUTLET 34, при условии, что ваш магнитофон подойдёт. Я всё ещё сталкиваюсь с тем, что многие игры просто не загружаются с одного из моих магнитофонов.

Утилиты в машинном коде запускаются крайне редко. В теории большинство программ можно заставить работать, приложив массу навыков и опыта, но большинство пользователей обнаружили, что очень малая часть их программ для Spectrum (за исключением коммерческих игр, запускаемых через эмулятор вроде EMUTILITY) работает на SAM.
